name: Slabberjan
description: Slabberjan is a traditional Dutch elimination game, specific to Zeeland, where players swap 'pieces' (originally cards, now custom tiles/tokens called 'Doppen') to avoid holding the lowest rank at the end of a round. It is remarkably similar to the card game 'Gnav' or 'Cuckoo'. The game involves bluffing, special 'Matador' pieces that block swaps (Knight, Bird, Cat, Inn), and a pot that the loser must pay into. The last player with chips wins.
deck: 42 unique 'Doppen' (2 sets of 21 designs) or adapted 42-card deck

history.origins: Derived from the 18th-century card games 'Gnav' (Danish) and 'Vogelspiel' (German). When cards were banned/taxed, players switched to wooden pieces.
timeline: 1800s: Zeeland farmers adopt the game as 'Slabberjan'.
Present: A cherished folklore tradition in Walcheren.
history.cultural: Played in pubs with heavy wooden pieces slamming on tables. The loser pays the 'pot' often used for drinks.
history.evolution: The pieces (Bird, Cat, Inn) retained the old card imagery (Owl, Cat, Tavern).

setup.players: From two up to twenty or more in the parent game Gnav; the Zeeland variant Slabberjan is typically played with five to fifteen players for the best experience. Since each player receives one piece from the set of 42, two to forty-two players are possible.
setup.deck: 42 pieces. Ranking: Knight (Kap-af) > Bird > Cat > Inn > 12 > 11... > 0 > White Bread > Pot > Face > Fool (Jan Rit).
setup.dealing: Each player draws 1 piece from a bag. Kept secret.

rules.objective: Avoid having the lowest piece. Survive with chips.
rules.gameplay: Each player receives one piece from the bag (or deck), kept secret. Starting left of the dealer and going clockwise, each player may keep their piece (stand) or offer to swap with their left-hand neighbour. The neighbour must accept the swap unless they hold a matador (Knight, Bird, Cat, or Inn). Knight stops trading and the swap attemptor pays a token; Bird refuses with no penalty; Cat undoes all swaps so far; Inn forces the attemptor to swap with the next player instead. The dealer may swap with a piece drawn from the bag. When the swap round ends, everyone reveals; the player with the lowest piece pays one token to the pool. Fool (Jan Rit) is lowest; its holder must knock; both fool-holder and next-lowest pay. Last player with chips wins.
keyRules: One piece per player per round, drawn from bag.
Swap round: stand or swap with left neighbour; matadors (Knight, Bird, Cat, Inn) may refuse or trigger special effects.
Lowest piece pays one token; fool has special rules.
Elimination: players who lose all tokens drop out.

strategy.basic: If you have a high piece (12, 11, 10), keeping is usually safe. If you have a low piece (0, Pot, Fool), you MUST swap. The danger lies in the middle pieces (5, 6, 7)â€”swapping might get you a Matador (death) or a lower piece.
strategy.intermediate: Reading Neighbors: If the player to your right swaps with you and gives you a Fool, you are now desperate. You must swap to your left. If your left neighbor looks confident (Matador?), you are trapped.
strategy.advanced: The 'Blieken' Bluff: Pretending to hesitate with a high piece to catch a neighbor swapping.
tips: The 'Inn' forces you to bypass the holder.

variations.name: Gnav (Norwegian/Danish)
variations.description: Original Norwegian and Danish game with slightly different piece names and order: Cuckoo (stops trading), Knight (cut off), Cat (undo swaps), Horse, House (pass to next). Played with 42 cards or pawns; 2 to 20 or more players.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Gnav differs in piece names and order; engine constants match base game; no overrides needed for this variant.

variations.name: Slabberjan (Zeeland)
variations.description: Zeeland variant with Ruiter/Kap-af (knight), Vogel (bird), Poesje (cat), Herberg (inn); no horse; White Bread below zero. Played with 42 pieces only.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Zeeland variant uses same engine; piece names are regional; no engine overrides required.
